intro.text: The Lord Admiral, Taisha of the Helm, who drinks without pause and votes against Lord Merchant Vey on every question.
The Lord Admiral of the Helm, a powerless figurehead post that cost him his fortune; he drinks the Helm's wine to spite the Shipowners' Circle that put him there.
A former Lord Admiral of the Helm who turns the tables on the Shipowners' Circle and uses the leverage to help the Diem.

items.text: As a young Guild merchant Delius came close to being Lord Merchant, but sank his fortune into a lakstone mine with Vey. After five barren years he sold out to Vey, who struck a vein a week afterwards. Delius moved to the Helm and built a great fleet, until the Shipowners' Circle took it by making him Lord Admiral, a post that let him own nothing. Plotting revenge, he had his son, posing as his steward, buy a new fleet.

Delius loathed Vey and voted against him on every matter, whatever the cost to himself or the Helm; in the Taishin's first vote on the Diem, he alone voted to keep it. When Kenton called, Delius had just waved off two Helm messengers sent to curb his drinking, and told Kenton he would vote however Vey did not.

He threw a ball in Kenton's honour, where he rose, slurring, to pledge his vote to the Diem, and then collapsed. Afterwards he warned Kenton and Khriss that the A'kar meant to cut Lossand's trade unless it gave up its sand masters, and hinted that Kenton did not understand what a Lord Admiral was.

From the Helm's charter Kenton learned that the Lord Admiral was a figurehead named by the Shipowners' Circle, who could own nothing and got only a house, a ship on request and unlimited food and drink. Delius's lavish drinking was his revenge.

When dockmaster NaiMeer barred Kenton from sailing, Delius commandeered a ship and took him to Lraezare. There Lokkall said the Circle had removed him. Delius signed papers making the fleet his, threatened to close Kezare's port for a month, and had the Circle name Lokkall Lord Admiral, holding Lokkall's goods until he voted for the Diem.
On the voyage home he wanted to throw the dead attackers in the river, but let Ais give them a Kerztian burial. He attended the duel and the vote to make sure Lokkall kept his side of the deal.

appearance.text: Long brown hair and stubble; a blue coat over a white shirt and brown trousers, with an ornamental sword slung from a long shoulder strap.

personality.text: Rarely without a drink, a habit he calls wasting wine.
